 Veterans Day Closings Announced Across Wayne County; Mount Olive Releases Holiday Schedule
 By Amy Roux 
 Nov 8, 2026 | 10:51 PM 
 GOLDSBORO, N.C. — Americans across the nation will pause on Wednesday, November 11, to honor the brave men and women who have served in the United States Armed Forces as the country observes Veterans Day.
 In recognition of the federal holiday, schools, city and county government offices, banks, and postal services in Goldsboro and Wayne County will observe holiday closures.
 Veterans Day is observed annually on November 11 and serves as an opportunity to recognize the courage, sacrifice, and dedication of military veterans who have served during times of war and peace.
 Veterans Day Closures
 Residents should plan ahead for the following holiday closures:
 Schools: Wayne County public schools and many other educational institutions will be closed in observance of Veterans Day.
 City Government: City of Goldsboro administrative offices and nonessential government services are expected to be closed.
 County Government: Wayne County government offices will be closed for the holiday.
 United States Postal Service: Post offices will be closed, and regular mail delivery will be suspended. Priority Mail Express service may still be available.
 Banks: Many banks and financial institutions will be closed, although ATMs, online banking, and mobile banking services will remain available.
 Residents are encouraged to check with individual offices, schools, and businesses for specific holiday schedules. Emergency services will continue operating.
 Town of Mount Olive Announces Veterans Day Schedule
 The Town of Mount Olive has announced that its administrative offices will be closed on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 , in observance of Veterans Day.
 Town offices will reopen for regular business on Thursday, November 12, at 8 a.m. 
 Despite the holiday closure, several town services will continue operating on their regular schedules.
 Recyclable Center: Regular operating hours will not be affected by the holiday.
 Household Garbage Collection: Collection will continue as normally scheduled.
 Yard Waste Collection: Collection will continue on its regular schedule.
 Residents experiencing a water or sewer emergency during the holiday closure should call 919-658-5031 and select Option 0 to be connected with non-emergency dispatch.
 Town officials encourage residents to plan accordingly and wish everyone a safe Veterans Day holiday.
 Honoring Those Who Served
 Originally known as Armistice Day, November 11 marked the end of fighting in World War I in 1918. The holiday was later renamed Veterans Day in 1954 to recognize American veterans of all wars.
 Unlike Memorial Day, which specifically honors military personnel who died while serving their country, Veterans Day recognizes all who have served in the United States Armed Forces, both living and deceased.
 For Goldsboro and Wayne County, Veterans Day holds special significance because of the community’s longstanding military connections, including Seymour Johnson Air Force Base and the many veterans and military families who call the area home.
 Goldsboro Veterans Day Parade
 The community will have an opportunity to show its appreciation during the Goldsboro Veterans Day Parade on Wednesday, November 11.
 The parade is scheduled to begin at 11:11 a.m. , with participants lining up at 9:30 a.m. near South Center and Spruce streets.
 The parade route will travel through downtown Goldsboro, turn around at Ash Street, and conclude near Chestnut Street.
 Residents are encouraged to attend, wave American flags, and show their appreciation for the veterans who have served our country.
 Whether attending a Veterans Day ceremony, thanking a veteran personally, or displaying an American flag, Wednesday offers an opportunity to reflect on the sacrifices made by those who have defended our nation’s freedoms.
 Goldsboro Daily News joins the community in thanking all veterans for their service, sacrifice, and dedication to our country.
